after.query: A Singaporean employee is age 32 and earns S$5,000 per month. Calculate the full salary and CPF contribution for September 2026.
after.message:
### Statutory Payroll & CPF Assessment: Monthly Payroll & Statutory CPF Accrual (30 Sep 2026)

**Governing Authorities**: **MOM, CPF Board & IRAS** | **Legislation**: **Employment Act 1968 Section 22** & **Central Provident Fund Act 1953 §7 / First Schedule**

---

#### 1. Statutory Proration & Entitlement (MOM Employment Act 1968 Section 22)
* **Contracted Basic Monthly Salary**: **SGD 5,000.00**
* **Statutory Working Days (Mon–Fri)**: **22 / 22 days (Full)**
* **MOM Incomplete Month Formula**:
  $$\text{Gross Salary Payable} = \frac{\text{Monthly Basic Rate of Pay}}{\text{Total Working Days in Month}} \times \text{Actual Working Days Worked}$$
* **Gross Prorated Salary Payable**: $\mathbf{SGD\ 5,000.00}$

---

#### 2. Statutory CPF & Net Salary Breakdown (Central Provident Fund Act 1953 & 2026 Ceilings)
* **Gross Salary Subject to CPF (Ordinary Wage)**: **SGD 5,000.00** *(Within 2026 OW ceiling of SGD 8,000)*
* **Employee CPF Contribution (20%)**: $\mathbf{SGD\ 1,000.00}$ *(Statutory Rule: Cents discarded per Central Provident Fund Act 1953 Section 7)*
* **Employer CPF Contribution (17%)**: $\mathbf{SGD\ 850.00}$ *(Statutory Rule: Total rounded to dollar)*
* **Total CPF Payable to CPF Board (37%)**: $\mathbf{SGD\ 1,850.00}$
* **Net Take-Home Salary Payable to Staff**: $\mathbf{SGD\ 4,000.00}$ *(Gross SGD 5,000.00 - Employee CPF SGD 1,000.00)*
* **Skills Development Levy (SDL)**: **SGD 11.25** *(0.25% of gross remuneration payable by employer)*

---

#### 3. Singapore Tax Deductibility & MOM Compliance (IRAS & MOM)
* **100% Tax Deductibility**: Under **Section 14(1) and Section 14(1)(e) of the Income Tax Act 1947**, staff salaries (**SGD 5,000.00**) and mandatory employer CPF (**SGD 850.00**) are fully tax-deductible expenses in Form C-S.
* **Disbursement Timeline**: Under **Section 21(2) of the Employment Act 1968**, all outstanding salary must be disbursed to the employee on their last day of employment.

---

### Single Compound Journal Entry (30 Sep 2026)

* **Debit**: **Staff Salaries & Wages (P&L - Operating Expense)** — **SGD 5,000.00**
* **Debit**: **Employer CPF Contribution (P&L - Operating Expense)** — **SGD 850.00**
* **Credit**: **CPF Payable to CPF Board (Current Liability)** — **SGD 1,850.00**
* **Credit**: **Net Salaries Payable / Staff Clearing (Current Liability)** — **SGD 4,000.00**

**Balance Check**: $\text{Total Debits (SGD } 5,850.00) == \text{Total Credits (SGD } 5,850.00) \quad \checkmark\ \mathbf{Balanced}$

citations.title: MOM Formula for Salary Computation for Incomplete Month of Work
citations.text: Under Section 22 of the Employment Act 1968, salary for an incomplete month of service (commencement, resignation, or termination) is calculated as: (Monthly Basic Salary / Total Working Days in Month) x Total Working Days Worked.

citations.title: Statutory CPF Contribution Rates & Rounding Rules (Cents Discarded for Employee, Dollar Rounding for Employer)
citations.text: Under Section 7 and the First Schedule of the Central Provident Fund Act 1953, the employer pays both employer and employee contributions. The employee share is deducted from wages with cents discarded. The total contribution is rounded to the nearest dollar, and employer contribution is the difference between total and employee contribution.

citations.title: Ordinary Wage (OW) Monthly Ceiling ($8,000 in 2026) & Additional Wage (AW) Ceiling
citations.text: CPF contributions are payable on Ordinary Wages (OW) up to the statutory monthly wage ceiling, and on Additional Wages (AW) up to the annual ceiling formula.

citations.title: Tax Deductibility of Statutory Employer CPF Contributions
citations.text: Mandatory employer contributions made in respect of an employee to the CPF pursuant to the CPF Act are allowable as deductions in determining taxable corporate profit.

citations.title: Statutory Salary and Overtime Payment Timelines (Within 7 / 14 Days)
citations.text: An employer must pay salary to employees at least once a month and within 7 days after the end of the salary period. Overtime pay must be paid within 14 days after the salary period.

citations.title: Skills Development Levy (SDL) Calculation Formula (0.25%, Min $2, Max $11.25)
citations.text: Employers must pay a monthly Skills Development Levy (SDL) for all employees rendering services in Singapore, collected by the CPF Board on behalf of SkillsFuture Singapore.

rationalePoints: Under MOM Employment Act §22: Gross prorated salary = (SGD 5,000 / 22 working days) * 22 days worked = SGD 5,000.00.
Under CPF Act §7: Employee CPF share (20%) is SGD 1000. Cents ($0.00) are discarded per statute.
Under CPF Act §7: Employer CPF share (17%) is SGD 850. Total CPF contribution (SGD 1850) is rounded to nearest dollar.
Net Take-Home Salary = Gross Salary ($5,000.00) - Employee CPF ($1000) = SGD 4,000.00.
Under Section 14(1)(e) of the Income Tax Act 1947: Mandatory employer CPF ($850) is 100% tax-deductible.
